budget_items.topic: Open space plan extension / grant eligibility
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported the state approved extending the open space plan from a seven-year to a 10-year plan, valid through fiscal year 2029, which lets the committee keep applying for open space grants through June 2029 without redoing a plan update next year.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 61/61A/61B tax status on 222 West Towns Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair explained that landowners in chapter 61 (forestry), 61A (agriculture) or 61B (conservation/recreation) get a lower tax rate, and if they sell for development they exit chapter status, pay back taxes, and the town gets a right of first refusal to match a sale price.

minutes.summary: The Open Space Committee welcomed two new members (from the Parks Commission and Planning Board), approved minutes from a prior joint meeting, and unanimously voted to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 13-acre Chapter 61 parcel at 222 West Towns Road, finding it did not meet the committee's open-space criteria. what_happened.line: The committee voted 5-0 to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 13-acre Chapter 61 parcel at 222 West Towns Road.
The chair reported the state extended the town's open space plan through fiscal year 2029, keeping it eligible for open space grants without an update next year.
Members took on reviewing the town master-plan steering committee's spreadsheet individually ahead of the next meeting, agreeing not to deliberate on it by email.
The next meeting was moved from September 10th to September 3rd, on Zoom, due to the chair's surgery and the vice chair's travel.

why_it_matters: The Select Board still decides whether to exercise the right of first refusal; this recommendation means the parcel is expected to proceed toward private sale rather than town purchase or protection as open space.
The plan extension keeps the town eligible for state open-space grant funding through 2029 without requiring a new planning cycle next year.
Residents watching the town's master plan process will see committee input feed into that steering committee's work following the September review.
